Thanks @averinevg for catching this!

Confirmed — these four new files were developed as part of my AMD employment responsibilities, and AMD is the appropriate copyright holder.

I've updated all four files to use the AMD copyright attribution and MIT SPDX headers in commit `64214f2`.

This is a headers-only change; no implementation or regression-test logic was modified.

Thanks for the review!

[SUGGESTION] Comments that only make sense with the author's external evidence repo. Examples: "verified by Phase-3 canary G57-7 on gfx1151/hiprtc 7.14" (`miopen_freestanding_initializer_list.hpp` ~29) and "adversarial reviews F1, V1" (test ~119). Drop them.

Addressed in 1845028f: the comment now states the underlying constraint (clang lowers braced-init-lists to field stores on this exact layout, so field order and types are fixed by the ABI) without the reference to my external validation setup.
[SUGGESTION] The non-RTC branch still includes `<limits>`, but `numeric_limits` is no longer used. The two adjacent `#ifdef` / `#ifndef MIOPEN_HIP_RUNTIME_COMPILE` blocks can also be merged.

Addressed in 1845028f: <limits> dropped (numeric_limits is no longer used — encode() works from the predefined __INT32_MAX__/__INT64_MAX__ macros) and the two adjacent MIOPEN_HIP_RUNTIME_COMPILE guards merged into one include block. The runtime-compile arm is unchanged. MIOpenKthvalue.cpp — the only radix.hpp consumer — was recompiled through the production AddKernel path in both the ambient and STL-isolated quadrants; both produce a code object.
Please use the existing runtime-compilation test infrastructure, e.g. gtests like `gtest/handle_test.cpp` or `gtest/miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp`, instead of a standalone hipRTC test.

Thanks for the guidance — the regression test now lives in MIOpen's existing gtest runtime-compilation infrastructure and the standalone binary plus its manual CMake registration are gone (commit 1d2481cf; the two smaller thread comments are addressed in 1845028f).

**Design.** `test/gtest/hiprtc_selfcontained.cpp` registers `CPU_HipRtcSelfContained_NONE.RtCompilesBatchNormWithoutHostStl` through the normal gtest glob (no custom CMake), and compiles the *embedded production* `MIOpenBatchNormFwdTrainSpatial.cpp` through `Handle::AddKernel` — the same pathway `handle_test.cpp` / `miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp` use — so the fix is exercised through its real wiring (option assembly, embedded kernel sources, named-header include map), and the target architecture comes from the live device.

**Keeping the original guarantee.** The host C++ standard library is made unreachable by passing `-nostdinc` (fallback `-nostdinc++`) in the compile options, and a paired probe proves it before any verdict counts: a negative probe that `#error`s when any of `<type_traits>/<utility>/<limits>/<initializer_list>` is still reachable, plus a positive ambient probe that actually uses `<type_traits>`. On a tree where a kernel header regresses to host-STL includes, the runtime compile fails and the test fails. A per-run compile option defeats the kernel-binary cache (keyed by program+options), so a stale cached object can never satisfy it.

**Results (Windows 11, gfx1151, ROCm 7.14 wheel toolchain):**
- patched tree: PASS — probes prove isolation, the BatchNorm kernel compiles with no host STL reachable, the code object loads; the with-STL control also passes;
- unpatched baseline (`54b079ca` + this test): FAILS with the original field signature — `miopen_type_traits.hpp:151: fatal error: 'type_traits' file not found` as the single error — while the same kernel compiles with STL available, i.e. the failure is STL-specific;
- hosts whose runtime compiler injects host STL anyway (e.g. comgr on Linux) skip with an explicit message that the no-STL condition was not tested — never a silent pass; inconsistent probe results fail the test instead of guessing.

One conscious trade vs the standalone: the test now runs through a live `Handle` like the other runtime-compilation gtests, so it needs a GPU present and no longer doubles as a GPU-less compile-only checker. The wheel environment this regression targets always has the GPU; the no-STL condition itself is the compiler environment, recreated by the isolation flags and verified by the probes.

Threads on the comment cleanup and radix.hpp `<limits>` are addressed in 1845028f: `MIOpenKthvalue.cpp` (the only radix.hpp consumer) was recompiled through the production path in both the ambient and STL-isolated quadrants. Happy to adjust anything else.

I suggest renaming `miopen_freestanding_initializer_list.hpp` to `miopen_initializer_list.hpp` and moving the header selection logic into it. Then `tensor_view.hpp` only needs `#include "miopen_initializer_list.hpp"`.

Done: renamed to `miopen_initializer_list.hpp` and moved the header selection into it (real `<initializer_list>` when reachable, freestanding definition otherwise); `tensor_view.hpp` now only includes it and the CMake kernel-header registration was updated (c6ed8131). The fallback layout is unchanged; the regression test brace-constructs `tensor_layout_t` and verifies the written values on GPU.

The `miopen_cstdint.hpp` include doesn't add much on its own here, since `MIOpenKthvalue.cpp` (the only user) already includes it, both directly and via `tensor_view.hpp`, before `radix.hpp`. Including what you use is a good idea, but then I think it would be worth adding the rest as well, e.g. `miopen_type_traits.hpp` for `std::is_same`.

Done: kept `miopen_cstdint.hpp` and added `miopen_type_traits.hpp`, so `radix.hpp` now directly includes what it uses; both headers are mode-self-selecting, so the includes are unconditional while the HIP headers stay in the offline branch (c6ed8131). kthvalue gtest re-run on gfx1151: 27/27 through the real runtime-compile path.
I think `miopen_utility.hpp` and `miopen_freestanding_utility.hpp` can be merged. Also we don't need to support `HIP < 7` anymore.

Done: merged — the `std::forward` fallback now lives inside `miopen_utility.hpp` under `!__has_include(<utility>)`, `miopen_freestanding_utility.hpp` is deleted and the HIP < 7 branch is gone (c6ed8131). The regression test exercises `std::forward` for an lvalue and an rvalue and checks the values the kernel writes.

Same idea as for `miopen_utility.hpp`: I think `miopen_type_traits.hpp` and `miopen_freestanding_type_traits.hpp` can be merged. Since HIP < 7 doesn't need to be supported anymore, the existing code here can be reused as the fallback, with the condition changed from the HIP version check to `!__has_include(<type_traits>)`.

Done: merged — the trait fallback from `miopen_freestanding_type_traits.hpp` now lives in `miopen_type_traits.hpp` under `!__has_include(<type_traits>)`, the HIP < 7 / `__hip_internal` code is removed, and the separate file is deleted (c6ed8131). The compile-time self-checks stay inside the fallback branch; validated on Windows gfx1151 with the no-STL leg passing.
I think the starting comment can be reduced
Done: reduced to a short lead paragraph plus one-line comments on each probe (f0f330c4).
I suggest the test compile a trivial inline kernel (like `miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp`) that uses the parts of the STL this PR adds.

Done: the test now compiles a trivial inline kernel in the style of `miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp` that includes `miopen_type_traits.hpp`, `miopen_utility.hpp` and `tensor_view.hpp` and uses `conditional_t`, `is_trivially_copyable_v`, `std::forward` (lvalue + rvalue) and brace construction of `tensor_layout_t`; the kernel launches and the host checks the written values (f0f330c4). The no-STL probe pair and the cache nonce are kept; on an unpatched tree the kernel fails with the original `'type_traits' file not found` signature (verified on gfx1151).
Nit: the explanations in ASSERT_TRUE, GTEST_SKIP and EXPECT_TRUE are quite long; a short line each should be enough.
Done: the ASSERT/GTEST_SKIP/EXPECT explanations are one-liners now (f0f330c4).
Nit: please drop this comment. The block itself is unchanged
Addressed in d4b574ac: comment removed, include block untouched. Verified: the diff shows only the two comment lines gone; kthvalue gtest re-run 27/27 on a fresh-cache build of the new head.

I think the partial-STL `#error` checks here and in `miopen_utility.hpp` can be dropped: `<type_traits>`, `<utility>` and `<initializer_list>` ship together in every standard library, and a broken mix would fail to compile anyway.

Addressed in d4b574ac: both #error blocks dropped (miopen_type_traits.hpp and miopen_utility.hpp); the `defined(MIOPEN_HIP_RUNTIME_COMPILE) && !__has_include(<...>)` selection conditions are unchanged, and the clang braced-init-list guard in miopen_initializer_list.hpp is untouched. Verified: no-STL gtest PASS on the new head; pristine-tree negative control still fails with the original `'type_traits' file not found` signature, so the regression test's detection power is unchanged.

Nit: the header comments in `miopen_utility.hpp`, `miopen_type_traits.hpp` and `miopen_initializer_list.hpp` can each be reduced to a line or two, e.g. "Minimal std::forward for runtime compilation without a host C++ standard library."

Addressed in d4b574ac: header comments in all three files reduced to 1–2 lines stating the technical purpose (miopen_utility.hpp uses your suggested wording verbatim; the initializer_list one keeps the single ABI constraint that explains the fixed field order). Verified: pre-commit/clang-format clean.

Please keep develop's definitions where they were, so the diff shows only the real changes. `integral_constant` / `true_type` / `false_type` moved to the top, but nothing before `is_same` uses them, so they can stay after `remove_cv` with just the HIP 6.x `#if` removed.
